brief: Goldman Sachs TMT specialist sales note ahead of the firm's San Francisco technology conference. It argues the two questions that decide the AI trade are AI monetisation and the durability of the capex cycle: Q2 fundamentals from Nvidia, Broadcom and Dell were strong but price action has been mixed, so what matters is whether managements can show compute demand, pricing and capacity still accelerating into 2027, and whether the buildout is reaching software and application-layer names. The desk reads positioning as friendly going in, with fundamental long/short gross leverage in the 27th percentile, net leverage in the 4th, and semiconductor implied volatility down from about 65 in July to 36. It expects Adyen to open lower on a report that Anthropic is assessing in-housing payments infrastructure, while noting Anthropic calls Stripe a key partner and near-term replacement is not implied. The remainder reports rather than argues: SIA July shipments, ASML's de-rating, raised optical transceiver forecasts, Samsung's tighter-2027 memory view, Apple's launch event, Vodafone's double upgrade against Cellnex's downgrade, and a desk view that AI borrowing is pressuring long-end yields.
